text:
Happy Friday evening! It's been another postcard autumn day, and the sunset at 5:55 should be a good one with clear skies and light wind. It cools off quickly after that. Tonight is mostly clear to partly cloudy with a low around 31, and I'd lean a little colder than that. The forecasters expect one of the chillier nights of the stretch, so plan on frost on the windshield and keep the jacket handy for the evening.

Tomorrow stays dry and sunny with a high near 55, a touch warmer than today and very calm, since high pressure sits right on top of us. Saturday night is clear and a bit milder, around 34.

Sunday is the pick of the weekend. Sunshine again, with a high near 61, and the models range from the upper 50s to low 60s. One TV forecast even has the low to mid 60s, so I'd bet on the warm side. Sunday night stays mild for late October, around 41. Zero rain in sight for the whole weekend.

A weak front slips through Monday, but the air is so dry it should only bring a few more clouds. Cooler Tuesday, then dry again. Get the outdoor chores and the leaf peeping done Saturday afternoon or Sunday.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-10-23T18:10:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Dry and quiet weather will continue into the start of next week, with seasonably warm temperatures expected
  2. Dry weather will persist much of next week with high pressure slowly crossing the region.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 210 PM EDT Friday... No significant changes have been made to the forecast.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: The stretch of dry and quiet weather will persist across the region as high pressure continues to build into the region, with the center of the high overhead tomorrow into Sunday before gradually shifting eastward. Ideal radiational cooling conditions will allow for some cold overnight lows tonight, with temperatures dropping into the teens and 20s, likely a few degrees cooler than the last few nights. Temperatures will gradually moderate throughout the weekend, with high temperatures warming into the lower 60s for Sunday and Monday. Dewpoints will be fairly low, dropping into the 20s or so, but no fire weather concerns are anticipated given the lack of winds across the region with the high pressure overhead. A weak cold front looks to move through the region on Monday, but with such dry air ahead of the feature and lack of moisture, no precipitation is expected just a slight increase in cloud cover. KEY MESSAGE 2: Our prolonged period of dry weather will continue through at least the middle part of next week as sprawling high pressure returns on Tuesday. Longer range models continue to show another cold frontal passage late week, accompanied by light QPF. Given the lack of a deep plume of moisture ahead of this front, wouldn't be surprised if we get nothing but a period of increased cloud cover, much like our frontal passage yesterday. Still, it's a week out, so have stayed with the NBM/WPC forecast for now, which gives low chances of showers late next week. Temperatures will remain seasonable, coolest on Tuesday but warming as the week progresses.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - We’ve entered day six of our gorgeous and sunny autumn stretch continues across Vermont and the North Country. High pressure settling overhead will keep skies clear and winds light, allowing for a chilly night tonight with lows in the upper 20s. Expect seasonable warmth to build back through the weekend, with highs reaching into the lower 60s by Sunday and Monday before a brief cool down Tuesday. Dry and quiet weather persists through the middle of next week as high pressure slowly crosses the region. Wednesday stays mostly sunny with highs near 51, warming back near 60 by Thursday under mostly sunny skies. A cold front may approach late next week with a slight chance for showers Thursday night into Friday, with highs near 57 on Friday, but confidence remains low with limited moisture available.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-23T15:51:00Z — same caveat): Sunny days continue through the weekend, gradually turning warmer — Friday will feature lots of sun and temperatures in the lower 50s! This weekend will continue to have lots of sunshine. Highs reach the 50s Saturday, rebounding to the low and mid-60s for Sunday. Despite the enjoyable stretch, we'll have to watch for worsening drought and an increased brush fire risk due to the prolonged dry pattern.
